headline: Tax windfall inflates earnings; segment margins diverge
summary_short: Gates' Q2 2026 revenue rose 6.5% y/y to $941.6M on volume and pricing gains across both segments, while diluted EPS more than tripled to $0.67 y/y — driven almost entirely by a $100.7M one-time discrete tax benefit tied to the Bermuda redomiciliation, not operations.
summary_long: Revenue rose 6.6% y/y (4.9% core, ex-FX) to $941.6M on volume and pricing gains in both segments. Power Transmission's Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 60bp to 22.9% on volume, pricing and manufacturing performance; Fluid Power's fell 120bp to 21.7% on lower volumes and inflation. Operating income rose 13.6% to $131.6M as gross-margin gains and a drop in restructuring costs (to $0.7M from $13.0M) outpaced higher SG&A. Net income jumped to $170.9M and diluted EPS to $0.67, almost entirely from a $100.7M one-time discrete tax benefit tied to the Bermuda redomiciliation — non-cash, non-recurring, and excluded from adjusted net income. Cash rose to $823.5M; H1 capex was $35.0M, buybacks $38.7M.

drivers.explanation: Driven by volume (+$23.1M) and pricing (+$19.8M) across both segments, aided by $15.0M of favorable currency translation; core sales grew 4.9% ex-FX, led by Power Transmission industrial-OEM strength.
The $32.0M increase was driven by higher volume (+$16.3M), inflation (+$7.8M) and tariffs (+$6.9M), partly offset by favorable manufacturing performance (-$6.5M).
Revenue growth of 6.6% outpaced cost-of-sales growth of 6.1%; company attributes the gap to favorable manufacturing performance and pricing outweighing inflation and tariffs.
Gross-profit growth combined with restructuring expense dropping to $0.7M from $13.0M outweighed a $19.5M SG&A increase driven by labor, FX and depreciation costs.
Tracks net income's 202.5% y/y jump on a diluted share count down only 1.7% from buybacks; nearly the entire move traces to the one-time tax benefit, not operations.

The rise in operating income was partly offset by $1.2M higher interest expense, while other expense fell $5.4M on a financing-related FX and hedging gain.

$100.7M of net discrete tax benefits — mainly $97.1M from a Luxembourg deferred-tax-asset realizability change tied to the Bermuda redomiciliation — flipped a $16.8M tax expense into a $78.0M tax benefit.
Built from $108.8M of H1 operating cash flow, partly offset by $41.8M used in investing (incl. $35.0M capex) and $50.8M used in financing (incl. $38.7M buybacks).
Retained earnings grew with six-month net income of $244.2M, partly offset by a wider accumulated other comprehensive loss and $38.7M of H1 share buybacks, per the equity statement.
Reflects the $38.7M H1 2026 share repurchase program reducing shares outstanding, per the cash-flow and equity statements.

MD&A attributes growth to personal-mobility and industrial-OEM demand and margin gains to productivity/pricing, flags the tax benefit as non-recurring, and discloses the pending Timken belts-business acquisition expected to close in H2 2026.
